QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_21

question.text: Antenatal-care (ANC) check-ups are a classic SAS-200 indicator. Which of the following is the STRONGEST MoV for ANC coverage?

answer.text: Count of ANC cards distributed by the NPO
Cross-verification of PHC / ASHA registers + Mother-and-Child Protection Card (MCP card) stamps + village-level ANC camp register
A single FGD with pregnant women in one village

explanation.text: The Logic: ANC coverage requires multi-source verification: PHC/ASHA register (administrative), MCP card (beneficiary-level document), and camp register (event-level). Triangulation is the gold standard under SAS-200. The Trap: Option A counts distribution not uptake. Option C has single-village single-tool bias. Option D is SE self-report. Cross-Exam Context: ASHA/PHC register cross-check is standard in health-impact evaluation treated in V-B (MF Foundation — health savings schemes) and cross-referenced in XII Ch 1. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Insist on ASHA register photocopies (masked for PII) for the engagement file. One PHC register gives you 40+ women's ANC data in one sheet.
